requirements.title: Take back a running turn only when the draft is empty, no heads are working, and the turn's own user message can be rewound
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Runtime/ThreadRuntime.swift:697-721 takeBackRunningTurn - guard draft.isEmpty, !hasWorkingHeads, currentTurnID, the turn, its userItemID, the entry, .user(message) and !message.isFromHydra, else interrupt() and return; then interrupt(); poll up to 200 times at 50 ms while phase != .idle; re-check phase == .idle, draft.isEmpty and the turn still present; revert(to: turnID, restoreFiles: false); on throw appendNotice(.error, "The stopped message was kept: \(error.localizedDescription)"); on success draft.text = message.text and draft.attachments = message.attachments
requirements.action: Escape in the composer.
requirements.expected_result: With all preconditions met the turn is stopped, the conversation and the provider context are rewound to before it with files left as the turn left them, and the message goes back into the composer as its text and attachments. Otherwise the turn is only interrupted and stays in the thread. The poll runs at most 200 iterations of 50 ms, i.e. ten seconds.
side_effects: Interrupts the provider session
Rewinds provider context via revert
On failure appends an error notice to the timeline
requirements.persistence: The thread's timeline is rewritten and saved by revert.
failure_cases: revert throws: the notice reads "The stopped message was kept: " followed by the localized error description, and the draft is not repopulated.
The user types while the stop lands: draft.isEmpty fails the re-check and the stopped turn stays in the thread.

requirements.title: Dragging the knob snaps to the nearest stop and fires an alignment haptic on each change
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Composer/EffortSlider.swift:801-818 DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) - the first change sets dragX inside .spring(response: 0.22, dampingFraction: 0.8), later changes set it directly; nearestStop is taken and, when it differs from the index, the index is written and NSHapticFeedbackManager performs .alignment at .now; onEnded clears dragX inside .spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.78)
DroppyCode/App/Views/Composer/EffortSlider.swift:833-836 nearestStop = min(count - 1, max(0, Int(((x - inset) / step).rounded())))
requirements.preconditions: A slider with two or more stops.
requirements.action: The user presses anywhere on the track and drags.
requirements.expected_result: A press with no movement already acts, because the minimum distance is zero: pressed on the track away from the knob, the knob springs to the pointer; pressed on the knob (within its 24 px radius of its drawn centre), it lifts to 1.06x where it is and never slides sideways (OD-0090). The knob follows the pointer, clamped to the insets, keeping the grip's offset when it was pressed on the knob (the source's knob centres on the pointer), and the selected index is the nearest stop to the knob's centre by rounding, so it changes as the centre passes the midpoint between two stops (OD-0090; the source rounds the pointer's position, which is the same except for the grip's offset). On the press the knob springs (response 0.22, damping 0.8): it lifts to 1.06x always, and slides to the pointer when it was pressed on the track; on release it springs onto the nearest stop and back to 1x (response 0.32, damping 0.78). The springs are the locked page's physical spring (work/design/jewel-knob-locked/jewel-knob.html:447-452: stiffness (2 pi / response)^2, damping 4 pi z / response), integrated in steps of at most 4 ms; a drawn frame moves them by the time since the last drawn frame, at most 50 ms (:813), so after a stall the knob goes on from where it was; the knob's drawn centre may pass either end's stop by at most 3 px while it springs (:586). Each index change fires an alignment haptic.
side_effects: Haptic feedback on each stop crossed
requirements.persistence: Through the binding, the thread's effort and the model preference.
failure_cases: count <= 1 or step <= 0: nearestStop returns 0.
requirements.cancellation: A cancelled gesture or a lost pointer capture releases the knob exactly as a release does: it springs onto the nearest stop and back to 1x (OD-0090; work/design/jewel-knob-locked/jewel-knob.html:556-557 pointerup, pointercancel and lostpointercapture all run the same release; the source leaves dragX set until the next gesture, with no cancellation handler).
requirements.windows_path: The springs are the locked page's, whose numbers are the source's (response 0.22 s, damping 0.8 held; 0.32 s, 0.78 released), applied as in expected_result; the drag keeps the grip's offset and rounds the knob's centre to the nearest stop (OD-0090). Haptics have no Windows equivalent and are dropped silently, never substituted with sound (port_impacts X8(e)).
requirements.verification_method: interaction test dragging across all stops

deviation.upstream: DroppyCode/App/Views/Composer/EffortSlider.swift:801-818 DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0): the first change sets dragX to the pointer's x inside .spring(response: 0.22, dampingFraction: 0.8) (:805), later changes set it directly (:807), nearestStop is taken of the pointer's x (:809, :833-836), and onEnded clears dragX inside .spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.78) (:815-816); the knob is scaled 1.06 while dragX is set (:795); there is no cancellation handler

The frame is taken at 0.5 seconds with a timescale of 600, deliberately not at the start, because a black first frame would otherwise become the thumbnail. requirements.title: Finder icons for non-media attachments are cached by a four-way key and bounded at 64 entries evicted oldest first
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Common/AttachmentPreview.swift:102-106 `/// Finder icons by extension, cached: one lookup per row per render stalled scrolling.` with `@MainActor enum FileIcons { private static var cache: [String: NSImage] = [:]; private static var order: [String] = [] }`

DroppyCode/UI/Common/AttachmentPreview.swift:108-120 `static func icon(for path: String) -> NSImage { let key = iconKey(for: path); if let hit = cache[key] { return hit }; let image = NSWorkspace.shared.icon(forFile: path); cache[key] = image; order.append(key); /* Bounded: icons are small but unbounded kinds are not. */ while order.count > 64, let oldest = order.first { order.removeFirst(); cache.removeValue(forKey: oldest) }; return image }`

DroppyCode/UI/Common/AttachmentPreview.swift:122-133 `private static func iconKey(for path: String) -> String { let ext = (path as NSString).pathExtension.lowercased(); if !ext.isEmpty { return ext }; var isDirectory: ObjCBool = false; if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: path, isDirectory: &isDirectory), isDirectory.boolValue { return "folder" }; if let type = try? URL(fileURLWithPath: path).resourceValues(forKeys: [.contentTypeKey]).contentType { return "type:\(type.identifier)" }; return "file" }`
requirements.preconditions: An attachment row needs a file icon.
requirements.action: The icon is requested for a path.
requirements.expected_result: The cache key is derived in four steps, in this order: the path's extension lowercased when it is non-empty; otherwise the literal "folder" when the path exists and is a directory; otherwise the literal "type:" followed by the resolved content type's identifier; otherwise the literal "file". Two files sharing an extension therefore share one icon, which is the point. On a miss the icon is read for that specific path and stored under the key. The cache is bounded at 64 entries and evicts in insertion order, oldest first, in a loop, so several entries over the bound are all evicted in one call. Insertion order is not refreshed on a hit, so this is first-in-first-out, not least-recently-used. The source records why the cache exists: one uncached lookup per row per render stalled scrolling.
side_effects: One system icon lookup per cache miss
requirements.windows_path: The bound of 64 and the first-in-first-out eviction are exact. The key derivation must keep its order: testing the extension first is what makes the cache useful, and the directory test must come before the content-type lookup because a directory has a content type too.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over a file with an extension, an extensionless file, a directory and 70 distinct kinds, asserting the keys and the eviction order

source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Diff/DiffInspector.swift:547-550 the doc comment on sync: 'Drives the popover from `runtime.isDiffVisible`. Call on change and on appear. Three cases: the composer moved to another thread (close what was open and never open on arrival), first appearance (adopt the runtime without opening unless asked), or the same thread (follow the flag as before).'

DroppyCode/App/Views/Diff/DiffInspector.swift:552-559 `if let current = self.runtime, current !== runtime { close(); if current.isDiffVisible { current.isDiffVisible = false }; self.runtime = runtime; seenOpenRequest = runtime.diffOpenRequest; if runtime.isDiffVisible, !CaptureRun.isEnabled { runtime.isDiffVisible = false }; return }`

DroppyCode/App/Views/Diff/DiffInspector.swift:560-567 the first-appearance branch: `if self.runtime == nil { self.runtime = runtime; seenOpenRequest = runtime.diffOpenRequest; if isVisible, !CaptureRun.isEnabled { runtime.isDiffVisible = false; return } }`

porting/dead_code.md entry 34 - DiffInspector.swift:557 and :563, the two `!CaptureRun.isEnabled` conjuncts inside DiffPopoverCoordinator.sync, are always true outside a capture launch, so adopting or switching to a runtime always forces runtime.isDiffVisible = false
requirements.preconditions: The composer's changes popover coordinator already serves one thread's runtime and the composer moves to a different thread.
requirements.action: sync is called with the new runtime.
requirements.expected_result: Three separate writes happen, in this order. First the popover is closed. Second, the OUTGOING runtime's isDiffVisible is set to false when it was true, so returning to the first thread later finds its changes panel closed rather than reopening it. Third, after adopting the new runtime and its open-request counter, the INCOMING runtime's isDiffVisible is set to false when it was true, so arriving at a thread that had the panel open does not open one. The second and third writes are separate observable state changes on two different runtimes, not one. The incoming clear is suppressed while website captures are enabled, so a capture run can arrive with the panel already open; the outgoing clear is not so guarded and always happens. The branch returns immediately and does not fall through to the follow-the-flag path. The first-appearance branch applies the same incoming clear, with the same capture guard.
side_effects: Writes isDiffVisible on two runtimes
Closes the popover
requirements.persistence: isDiffVisible lives on the runtime, not in user defaults.
requirements.windows_path: Both clears must be reproduced. Omitting the outgoing one leaves a thread that reopens its panel when you come back, which is a different product; omitting the incoming one pops a panel on every thread switch. The capture guard is dead code in every normal launch (porting/dead_code.md entry 34: the `!CaptureRun.isEnabled` conjuncts at DroppyCode/App/Views/Diff/DiffInspector.swift:557 and :563) and the capture subsystem is not ported (ED-001), so under ED-061 the port omits the guard and both clears are unconditional.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test moving between two threads, both with the panel open, asserting isDiffVisible on each runtime after the move and after moving back
requirements.b3_note: Citation only: B2's `WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled` (DiffInspector.swift:557, :563) is renamed `CaptureRun.isEnabled` at B3, at the same lines. No behaviour change; the capture subsystem stays unported under ED-001.

requirements.title: The changes popover adopts a new thread's open-request counter rather than treating the difference as a request to open
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Diff/DiffInspector.swift:593-594 `/// The thread's `diffOpenRequest` as last seen, so a counter that merely differs between two threads never opens the popover.` with `private var seenOpenRequest = 0`
DroppyCode/App/Views/Diff/DiffInspector.swift:556 the thread-switch branch's `seenOpenRequest = runtime.diffOpenRequest`
DroppyCode/App/Views/Diff/DiffInspector.swift:562 the first-appearance branch's `seenOpenRequest = runtime.diffOpenRequest`

DroppyCode/App/Views/Diff/DiffInspector.swift:596-603 `/// A tool row or a Review button bumped the request on the thread the coordinator already serves; a bump seen only because the composer moved to another thread is not an opener.` with `func reopen(runtime: ThreadRuntime) { guard runtime === self.runtime else { sync(isVisible: runtime.isDiffVisible, runtime: runtime); return }; guard runtime.diffOpenRequest != seenOpenRequest else { return }; seenOpenRequest = runtime.diffOpenRequest; desiredVisible = true; ... }`
requirements.preconditions: Each thread runtime carries its own monotonically bumped diffOpenRequest counter, and two threads hold different values.
requirements.action: The composer moves between threads, or a tool row or Review button bumps the counter.
requirements.expected_result: Whenever the coordinator adopts a runtime, on a thread switch and on first appearance alike, it copies that runtime's current open-request counter into its own last-seen value. A later reopen call therefore compares against the counter of the thread it is actually serving, and a value that merely differs because the composer moved to another thread is not treated as a request to open. A reopen call naming a runtime the coordinator is not serving does not open anything either: it is redirected into sync, which takes the thread-switch path. Only a bump on the thread already served, that is a value different from the adopted one, opens the panel, and that bump is then adopted in turn so it fires once.
side_effects: Opens the popover, but only for a genuine bump on the served thread
requirements.persistence: diffOpenRequest lives on the runtime; the last-seen value is coordinator state.
requirements.windows_path: A counter compared against a remembered baseline, adopted on every runtime change. Comparing against zero, or against the previous thread's value, makes every thread switch pop the changes panel.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test: two threads with different counters, moving between them with no bump (nothing opens), then bumping on the served thread (opens once), then moving away and back (nothing opens)

requirements.title: A video attachment's panel size is loaded asynchronously when its thumbnail appears, cached per path, and kept for the life of the process
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Common/AttachmentPreview.swift:253-257, the doc comment line by line: "/// The movie aspect-fitted into `imageBounds`, from the video track's natural size" / "/// (preferred transform applied), by path. The track is loaded with the modern async" / "/// API by the thumbnail's own task (see `prefetchVideoSize`); the panel sizes itself" / "/// before the player exists, so an unloaded track falls back to `imageBounds`.", then :264 "@MainActor private static var videoSizes: [String: CGSize] = [:]"

DroppyCode/UI/Common/AttachmentPreview.swift:259-272 `static func prefetchVideoSize(for attachment: Attachment) async { guard attachment.isVideo, videoSizes[attachment.path] == nil else { return }; let asset = AVURLAsset(url: attachment.url); guard let tracks = try? await asset.loadTracks(withMediaType: .video), let track = tracks.first, let (natural, transform) = try? await track.load(.naturalSize, .preferredTransform) else { return }; var size = natural.applying(transform); size = CGSize(width: abs(size.width), height: abs(size.height)); guard size.width > 0, size.height > 0 else { return }; let scale = min(imageBounds.width / size.width, imageBounds.height / size.height); videoSizes[attachment.path] = CGSize(width: floor(size.width * scale), height: floor(size.height * scale)) }`
DroppyCode/UI/Common/AttachmentPreview.swift:234 `static let imageBounds = CGSize(width: 480, height: 360)`
DroppyCode/UI/Common/AttachmentPreview.swift:210-211 its only caller, AttachmentVideoThumbnail's `.task(id: attachment.path) { await AttachmentLargePreview.prefetchVideoSize(for: attachment)`
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/TimelineRows.swift:1305-1306 `} else if attachment.isVideo { AttachmentVideoThumbnail(attachment: attachment, size: size)`, the one place the thumbnail is drawn
requirements.preconditions: A video attachment's thumbnail (AttachmentVideoThumbnail, drawn by AttachmentThumbnail for a video) appears in an attachment strip: the composer draft, a queued follow-up, a prompt editor or a sent message.
requirements.action: The thumbnail's task runs prefetchVideoSize for the attachment.
requirements.expected_result: When the attachment is a video and its path has no cached size, the first video track and its natural size and preferred transform are loaded asynchronously; the transform is applied, both sides are made positive, and the size is aspect-fitted into 480 by 360 with each side floored, then stored under the attachment's path. A path already cached, or a non-video attachment, returns at once with no load. The check comes before the two awaited loads and the store after them, so two runs for one path that overlap both load and each stores its result. No track, a failed load, or a zero width or height stores nothing, so the next run of the thumbnail's task tries again. The cache is keyed by path only, has no bound and no eviction, and lives for the life of the process, so a different file later placed at the same path keeps the first size.
side_effects: Reads the video file's track metadata whenever its path has no cached size when a run starts: runs that do not overlap read it once per path while it succeeds, but two runs for the same path whose loads overlap (for example the same file in the draft strip and in a sent message's strip) both read it, because the cache is checked before the awaited loads (:269) and written only after them (:278)
Grows an unbounded, process-lifetime path-to-size map
requirements.persistence: Nothing on disk; an in-memory map for the life of the process.
failure_cases: No readable video track, a failed load or a zero size: nothing is cached and a later run retries.
The thumbnail never appears: nothing is cached and the preview opens at 480 by 360 (PR-COMPOSER-210).
requirements.cancellation: Runs inside the thumbnail's .task(id: attachment.path), which SwiftUI cancels when the thumbnail goes away or its path changes; the source adds no cancellation handling of its own.
requirements.windows_path: An asynchronous media-metadata read of the first video stream's frame size and rotation, the rotation applied, sides made positive, fitted into 480 by 360 with floor, and stored in a process-lifetime dictionary keyed by path with no eviction. Start it from the video thumbnail's appearance, before the thumbnail's frame grab, as the source does; not from the preview's open.
requirements.verification_method: unit test of the fit over a landscape track, a portrait track rotated by its transform and a zero-size track, plus an integration test asserting one metadata read per path across two appearances that do not overlap, two reads for two appearances whose loads overlap, and a retry after a failed read
requirements.b2_change: New at B2. B1 had no cache: B1 DroppyCode/UI/Common/AttachmentPreview.swift:264-275 videoDisplaySize read `asset.tracks(withMediaType: .video).first` synchronously when the panel opened.
